title: Opening a PDF, page by page
kicker: Python for SDFs · Read the code

lines.title: Load the PDF library
lines.text: Loads PyMuPDF, the library that opens PDFs. In code it is called `fitz`, an old name that stuck.

lines.title: Open the file
lines.text: Opens the PDF you uploaded to Colab. `/content/` is the folder where Colab keeps uploads. `doc` now holds the whole document.

lines.title: Go page by page
lines.text: Visits each page in turn. `enumerate` hands you two things each time: a counter `i`, starting at 0, and the page itself.

lines.title: Ask the page for its text
lines.text: A method call: the page gives back all its text as one string, which is stored in `text`.

lines.title: Print a summary line
lines.text: An f-string fills in the values inside the curly brackets. `i + 1` turns the counter (0, 1, 2) into normal page numbers (1, 2, 3).

predict.question: The sample SDF has 3 pages. When this code runs, what does the **first** printed line start with?

options.label: Page 0:
options.feedback: Close, but `i` starts at 0 and the code prints `i + 1`, so the first number is 1.

options.label: Page 1:
options.feedback: Yes. `enumerate` starts `i` at 0, and the f-string prints `i + 1`, so the first line says Page 1.

options.label: page 1:
options.feedback: Look at the f-string again: the text inside the quotes is "Page", with a capital P, and Python prints it exactly.

options.label: An error
options.feedback: Every line here is valid Python, as long as the PDF exists at that path. It runs fine.
